answer: Divergent-Commitment Challenge. Each agent periodically commits to a private random seed, then must answer live queries derived from prior commitments. Honest agents hold unique seeds and can spiral into fresh responses; a clone sharing the same seed state produces identical answers, which the protocol flags as non-divergent. Attackers must maintain independent state and compute per identity, and detection forces costly re-seeding. Marginal cost rises toward a zenith where mass duplication is infeasible. No marble of trust is wasted on clones.
